existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `ResearchElementDefinition` is not present as an R6 resource. Top migration concerns are: existing R4 instances fail at the resource-type level; the likely `EvidenceVariable` successor is not a one-to-one rename; and R4's required PICO `type` plus mandatory `characteristic` model require semantic remapping. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official ConceptMap or migration narrative.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: R4-to-R6 migration must choose a new evidence-domain representation, most plausibly involving R6 `EvidenceVariable` and sometimes `Evidence`, `Group`, or extensions. A mechanical `resourceType` replacement will not work because old fields such as `type`, `variableType`, `characteristic`, `subject[x]`, `usage`, `library`, and parts of `relatedArtifact` have no same-path R6 target. R6-to-R4 round-tripping is also risky because R6 EvidenceVariable permits instances without R4-required `status`, `type`, or `characteristic`, and it can express data-storage, constraint, and missing-data semantics that R4 ResearchElementDefinition cannot carry.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same-name R6 artifact is absent: the assigned file is missing, the R6 package index has no StructureDefinition entry, and `fhir-old-types` identifies the name as old. Confidence is medium for exact replacement guidance because `EvidenceVariable` is only a candidate successor inferred from local definitions and purpose text, not an official ConceptMap. Terminology and semantic confidence would improve with official expansions and migration notes.

rationaleMd:
ResearchElementDefinition has a resource-identity break: ResearchElementDefinition resource is absent from the R6 core package. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 94/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.
